prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1081; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep it to the case caption, if that's all right. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: That's fine for today. Do you understand you're under oath, the same as if you were in court?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Good. Tell me about the afternoon of the collision. Where were you headed?

A: I was driving home from a client meeting. I was in the left-turn lane at a signalized intersection in Houston, waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic.

Q: What happened when you started the turn?

A: The light had turned green for me, and I started into the intersection. A pickup coming straight through the intersection hit the driver's side of my car. I didn't see it coming until right before impact.

Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?

A: I don't think I fully blacked out, but I was dazed. I remember the airbag going off and a ringing in my ears. Things were foggy for a while after that.

Q: What was the first medical care you received?

A: The paramedics checked me at the scene and asked me a lot of questions about what day it was and where I was. Then I was taken to the emergency room, where they did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion.

Q: Since the accident, what treatment have you received?

A: I've seen my primary care doctor several times, and I was referred to a neurologist. I've also done some vision therapy and a few sessions with a physical therapist for my neck and shoulder. I still get headaches most days, and bright screens make them worse.

Q: Have you missed any work because of your symptoms?

A: Yes. For the first several weeks I couldn't look at a computer for more than a few minutes at a time, so I was out of the office and working reduced hours when I could. My employer has been accommodating, but I know my productivity has suffered.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life outside of work?

A: I used to run a few times a week and play in a weekend recreational league. I've had to stop both. Reading is harder, I lose my train of thought, and I've been more irritable with my family. My spouse has had to take on more of the household chores, and I've canceled plans with friends because I'm just wiped out by the evening.

Q: Do you have any prior head injuries or conditions affecting your concentration or headaches?

A: I had a minor fall years ago that I didn't think much about. Other than that, I had no regular headaches before this accident.

Q: Is there anything else about your symptoms you'd like to add to your testimony today?

A: Only that some days are better than others, and I'm still hopeful I'll get back to normal. I'm working with my doctors on it.
